post.description:
Creates one post on one social account.

- `status: draft` (default) saves a draft.
- `status: scheduled` with `scheduled_at` schedules it at that time; with `queue` (`next` or `top`) it takes a slot of the channel's posting schedule; with `queue_slot` it takes that exact free slot (from `GET /channels/{account}/queue/slots`).
- `status: publishing` publishes it now.

Omitted `content_type` is chosen like the app does: on Pinterest a video makes `pinterest_video_pin` and several images `pinterest_carousel`, on TikTok images only make `tiktok_photo`, every other network takes its default format.

To schedule or publish, the post needs its network's required settings in `meta` (see `PlatformMeta`). Sending `platforms` is refused with `422`; validation errors name the field directly (`meta.board_id`, `content_type`). API keys belong to workspace admins, who publish directly, so a post created through the API is never stored as `pending_approval`.

To post the same text on several channels at once, use `POST /posts/batch`.

content.description: Post text, at most 25000 characters. When `status` is `scheduled` or `publishing` it must also fit each account's limit (`max_content_length` of the social account, for example 280 on X or 25000 for X accounts with long posts, 300 on Bluesky, 500 on Mastodon including the content warning), measured on the text the network receives. A scheduled or published post needs text or media.

media.description: Media in order. Each item is one of `upload_token`, `url` or `id`. Types the channel does not accept are refused.

status.description: `draft` keeps the post editable. `scheduled` schedules it at `scheduled_at` or in the channel queue (`queue`). `publishing` publishes it now.

social_account_id.description: Social account of this workspace. A post has exactly one; use `POST /posts/batch` for several.

content_type.description: Format; must belong to the account's network. Omitted, it is chosen from the media.

scheduled_at.description: When to publish, for `status: scheduled`. Any date string; must be in the future and before `2038-01-19`. Cannot be combined with `queue`. Required with `status: scheduled` unless `queue` or `queue_slot` is sent.

queue.description: Queue position, only with `status: scheduled`. `next` takes the channel's first free slot; `top` takes its first slot and moves the queued posts behind it to the next gap. The channel must have posting times (`has_posting_schedule`). Cannot be combined with `scheduled_at`.

queue_slot.description: Instant of one free slot from `GET /channels/{account}/queue/slots`, only with `status: scheduled`. Stores the post as a queue post in that slot; refused when the slot is taken or held by a pending approval request. Before `2038-01-19`. Cannot be combined with `queue`. Takes the place of `scheduled_at` when both are sent.

put.description:
Updates a post. Only the fields you send change. The social account is fixed (`social_account_id` is refused), and so is `platforms`.

`content_type` and `meta` are top-level fields. `meta` is merged with the stored settings: send `null` for a key to clear it (string, list and object settings; boolean settings cannot be cleared, so send `true` or `false`); `thread_replies` replaces the whole list; `poll` is merged key by key, its `options` replaced as a list. Validation errors name the field directly (`meta.privacy_level`, `content_type`). `media` replaces the post's media; `label_ids` replaces its labels.

`status: publishing` publishes the post now; `scheduled` schedules it at `scheduled_at`, in the queue (`queue`), or keeps its future `scheduled_at`; `draft` unschedules it (it is no longer published; the last `scheduled_at` stays on the draft). When scheduling or publishing, the content type must fit the media and the required settings must be present.

Posts that are publishing, published or failed cannot be edited: the request returns `422` with `This post has already been processed and cannot be re-published. Duplicate it to try again.`

On this endpoint an invalid body may answer `422` before the `404` check of a post of another workspace.

content.description: Post text, at most 25000 characters. When `status` is `scheduled` or `publishing` it must also fit each account's limit (`max_content_length` of the social account, for example 280 on X or 25000 for X accounts with long posts, 300 on Bluesky, 500 on Mastodon including the content warning), measured on the text the network receives. A scheduled or published post needs text or media.

media.description: Replaces the post's media. Omit it to keep the current media. Media in order. Each item is one of `upload_token`, `url` or `id`. Types the channel does not accept are refused.

status.description: `draft` keeps the post editable. `scheduled` schedules it at `scheduled_at` or in the channel queue (`queue`). `publishing` publishes it now. Omit it to keep the current status.

content_type.description: New format for the post's channel. Omitted, the stored format is kept, except on Pinterest and TikTok where new media decides it as on create.

meta.description: Settings of the post's channel, merged with the stored ones.

scheduled_at.description: With `status: scheduled`: required unless `queue` is sent or the post already has a future time; must be in the future and before `2038-01-19`. Cannot be combined with `queue`.

queue.description: Queue position, only with `status: scheduled`. `next` takes the channel's first free slot; `top` takes its first slot and moves the queued posts behind it to the next gap. The channel must have posting times (`has_posting_schedule`). Cannot be combined with `scheduled_at`. Refused on posts with several destinations.

post.description:
Approves a post waiting for approval (`pending_approval`). With an empty body the post is scheduled as requested: in the queue position or at the time the member asked for. Send `scheduled_at` to pick another time, or `publish_now` to publish it now. When the requested time has passed (or the member asked to publish now) and neither is sent, the request fails with `422` on `scheduled_at`: `The requested time has passed. Choose a new time.` A post that is no longer pending fails with `422`: `This post is no longer waiting for approval.` The member who asked is emailed about the decision.

API keys belong to workspace admins, who publish directly, so posts created or edited through the API never wait for approval. These endpoints decide the requests of members who need approval.

post.description: Uploads one file as `multipart/form-data` without a post and returns an `upload_token`. Pass it as a media item (`media[].upload_token`) to `POST /posts`, `POST /posts/batch` or `PUT /posts/{post}`, or to `POST /posts/{post}/media/from-upload`, before `expires_at`. A token is spent by the first post that takes it; to put the same file on another post, pass that post's `media[].id`. Unused uploads are deleted after 24 hours. Accepted files: JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP images (HEIC and HEIF too when the server can convert them, stored as JPEG), MP4 and MOV videos, and PDF documents. Size caps: 10 MB per image (and at most about 67 megapixels, 8192 × 8192 pixels in total), 1 GB per video, 100 MB per PDF. Each network enforces its own, usually smaller, caps when the post is scheduled or published (`GET /content-types`).

Receives a file at a one-time signed URL issued by the MCP `request-media-upload-tool`. No API key: the signature authorizes the request. Send the file as `multipart/form-data` in the `media` field, for example `curl -F media=@launch.jpg "<upload_url>"`. The URL works once, until it expires (15 minutes by default); a second upload to it returns `409`. The returned `upload_token` is then used as a media item, like a token from `POST /uploads`. Accepted files: JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP images (HEIC and HEIF too when the server can convert them, stored as JPEG), MP4 and MOV videos, and PDF documents. Size caps: 10 MB per image (and at most about 67 megapixels, 8192 × 8192 pixels in total), 1 GB per video, 100 MB per PDF. Each network enforces its own, usually smaller, caps when the post is scheduled or published (`GET /content-types`). A file the server cannot read returns `422` with only `message`: `Unable to read uploaded file.`

get.description: Returns the channel's time zone, weekly posting goal and posting times. Queue slots (`queue: next|top`, `queue_slot`) come from these times, in the channel's time zone.

put.description: Replaces the channel's time zone, posting goal and posting times. Send all seven days, or `posting_schedule: null` to remove every posting time. Every field is written: omitting `posting_goal` or `posting_schedule` clears it like `null`, so send the current values to keep them (read them with `GET /channels/{account}/posting-schedule`). Without posting times, the channel's queued posts become custom-time posts at their current time. Queued posts keep their slot. A schedule change moves only the posts whose slot no longer exists, into the first free slots in order. A time zone change first gives each queued post the slot at the same local time in the new zone, then the first free slots; queue requests pending approval follow the same rule. A queued post with no slot left becomes a custom-time post at its current time. Custom-time posts never move.

posting_goal.description: Posts per week. `null` or omitted clears it: send the current value to keep it.

posting_schedule.description: Exactly seven days, each `day` once. `null` or omitted removes the posting times (queued posts become custom-time posts): send the current values to keep them.

post.description: Replaces the channel's posting times with `goal` times a week at the hours that usually work best on its network (minutes are randomized), and stores `goal` as the posting goal. Without `goal`, the channel's current goal is used, else 3. The time zone does not change. Every day ends up enabled. `mode` is required but has no effect today: both values generate the same schedule. Queued posts keep their slot. A schedule change moves only the posts whose slot no longer exists, into the first free slots in order. A queued post with no slot left becomes a custom-time post at its current time. Custom-time posts never move.

Copies the posting times of another channel of the workspace onto this one. The time zone and posting goal of this channel stay. A source whose `posting_schedule` is `null` returns `422` on `from`. A source with an empty schedule is copied as is, which removes this channel's posting times. Queued posts keep their slot. A schedule change moves only the posts whose slot no longer exists, into the first free slots in order. A queued post with no slot left becomes a custom-time post at its current time. Custom-time posts never move.

404.description: This channel or the `from` channel does not exist in this workspace.

get.description: Lists the channel's next free queue slots, soonest first: at most 30, within the next 90 days, and more than a minute away. A slot is taken when a scheduled post (queued or custom time) or a queue request pending approval holds it. Pass one as `queue_slot` on `POST /posts` or as `slot_at` on `PUT /channels/{account}/queue/slot`. Empty when the channel has no posting times.

put.description: Reorders the first queued posts of the channel. Send the ids of the first N queued posts (scheduled in queue mode, more than a minute away, in time order) in the new order: the posts swap among the times they already hold, and the posts after the first N stay where they are. When the ids are not exactly those first N posts (the queue changed), the request returns `422` on `post_ids`. Custom-time posts are not part of the queue.

Moves a scheduled post of this channel (queued or custom time) onto one of the channel's free slots, as a queued post. Take `slot_at` from `GET /channels/{account}/queue/slots`. A slot that is taken, not in the posting schedule, more than 90 days away or held by a pending request returns `422` on `slot_at`; so does a post that is not scheduled on this channel.

Creates an enabled webhook that sends the chosen post events to your endpoint. The response includes the `signing_secret`. The endpoint must be a public `http` or `https` URL: other schemes and private or local addresses are refused with `422` `This endpoint is not allowed.` on `endpoint`.

Each delivery is a JSON `POST` with the body `{id, type, data, created_at}` and the header `X-Webhook-Signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with the webhook's `signing_secret`. Compare it with your own HMAC of the body before trusting it. A delivery that does not get a 2xx answer within 10 seconds is retried twice, a minute apart. Redirects are not followed.

Searches the audio an Instagram account connected through Facebook (`instagram-facebook`) can put on a Reel: licensed music first, then original sounds. Without `q`, lists what is trending. With `q`, music is kept only when its title or artist contains every word (accents optional), because Instagram also answers with unrelated tracks. Send a result's `id` as `meta.audio.id` on an `instagram_reel` post.

Each answer is kept for 10 minutes per account, `type` and query, and a cached answer costs nothing. An uncached one counts against the workspace's 30 audio lookups per minute. This endpoint also counts against a limit of 60 requests per minute per user, shared with the other Pinterest, Discord, TikTok and Instagram lookup endpoints and with the same user's channel lookups in the TryPost app.

PlatformMetaGoogleBusiness.title: Google Business Profile
PlatformMetaGoogleBusiness.description: Settings for `google_business_post`. An `EVENT` or `OFFER` needs `event.title`, `event.start_date` and `event.end_date` (the title is the offer title), and cannot end before it starts.

call_to_action.description: Button on the post. Not on `OFFER`.

PlatformMetaNone.title: Telegram
PlatformMetaNone.description: Telegram (and Facebook reels and stories) take no settings.

PlatformMeta.description: Per-network settings of one destination. Pick the shape of the destination's network. Keys without a rule are dropped. Every known key is validated whatever the network, but only the keys of the destination's network are used when publishing. On update, `meta` is merged with the stored settings: send `null` for a key to clear it (string, list and object settings; boolean settings cannot be cleared, so send `true` or `false`); `thread_replies` replaces the whole list; `poll` is merged key by key, its `options` replaced as a list. Required to schedule or publish: TikTok `privacy_level`, Pinterest `board_id`, Discord `channel_id`, Google Business `event` on `EVENT`/`OFFER`, YouTube a title (`title` or the first line of the text), X `poll.options` (2 or more) and `poll.duration_minutes` on `x_poll`. `GET /content-types` lists the unconditional ones (TikTok, Pinterest, Discord) per network as `required_meta`.

Post.description: A post on one channel. Posts created together from several channels are independent posts that share a `post_group_id`.

post_group_id.description: Shared by the posts created in one batch.

content.description: Post text, stored as sent (posts written in the app hold the editor's HTML).

status.description: Lifecycle of the post in TryPost. `pending_approval` is a post a member who needs approval asked to schedule or publish. The outcome on the network is `publish_status`.

schedule_mode.description: `queue`: the post holds a slot of the channel's posting schedule. `custom`: it is scheduled at its own time.

approval_requested_by.description: Who asked for approval (not always the author).

remaining.description: Repeats left after the next one.

origin.description: `network` for posts imported from the network (published outside TryPost).

publish_status.description: Publishing state on the network. `pending` until the post is sent; `retrying` waits for a retry after a network limit; `pending_review` and `rejected` come from networks that review posts (Google Business).

meta.description: Stored per-network settings (see `PlatformMeta`). Empty settings may serialize as an empty array.

platform_url.description: Link to the published post on the network.

error_message.description: Why publishing failed, when it did.

display_name.description: Account name, kept even after the account is disconnected.

social_account.description: The account, or `null` once it was removed (the `display_*` fields keep its name).

examples.content: We just shipped scheduled threads. Here is how they work.

thread_replies.text: 2/ Replies publish under the first post.

PostNote.description: An internal note on a post. Notes are never published.

PublicationAnalytics.description: Saved analytics of one publication: the latest daily snapshot collected from the network.

post_id.description: TryPost post, or `null` for a post made outside TryPost.

voting_status.description: As X last reported it. `closed` only once a read after the end has seen it closed.

poll.description: X polls: the votes per choice, read with the post's other X metrics (about an hour after publishing, then at 2, 3, 7, 14 and 28 days). A poll made on x.com also gets them when it is discovered. `null` on any other post or before the first read.

thread_polls.description: X threads published by TryPost: the votes of each reply that is a poll. Empty otherwise.

voting_status.description: As X last reported it. `closed` only once a read after the end has seen it closed.

metrics.description: Metrics the network reports for this publication, keyed by metric. An empty array `[]` when no snapshot has been collected yet. Keys (`reactions`, `comments`, `views`, `impressions`, `reach`, `engagement_rate`, ...). Each value is an object.

platform_post_id.description: The post's id on the network.

metrics.description: The saved analytics, or `{unsupported: true, reason}` when there are none: `not_published`, `platform_not_supported` (LinkedIn, LinkedIn Page, Telegram, Discord and Google Business are not in analytics) or `not_collected` (not collected yet).

PostPreview.description: Without a channel only `post_id`, `original_content` and `original_length` are returned.

original_length.description: Characters (code points) of the stored content.

platform.description: Present only when the post has a channel, like the fields below.

sanitized_content.description: The text the publisher sends to the network.

max_content_length.description: Text limit of the account (an X account with long posts gets 25000; an X poll's question is capped at 280).

truncated.description: Whether the sent text is shorter than the stored text.

description_length_bytes.description: YouTube only. The limit is 5000 bytes.

poll.description: X `x_poll` only: the poll as it is sent (choices without blanks; a draft without a length shows 1440).

thread_replies.description: X, Bluesky and Mastodon, when the post has replies.

poll.description: X only, when the reply is a poll.

Upload.description: A temporary upload. Pass `upload_token` as a media item before `expires_at`.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601. 24 hours after the upload; unused uploads are then deleted.

id.description: Pinterest board id. Send it as `meta.board_id` on a Pinterest destination.

cover_url.description: Cover image of the board, when Pinterest has one.

id.description: Discord channel id. Send it as `meta.channel_id` on a Discord destination.

TikTokCreatorInfo.description: What TikTok allows this creator to publish right now.

can_post.description: `false` when TikTok answered that the creator cannot post now (no privacy options).

privacy_level_options.description: Values allowed for `meta.privacy_level` on this account.

comment_disabled.description: Comments are off in the creator's TikTok settings: `allow_comments` has no effect.

max_video_post_duration_sec.description: Longest video this creator may post, in seconds.

day.description: Day of the week: `0` is Sunday, `6` is Saturday. Send a JSON integer, not a string.

enabled.description: A disabled day keeps its times but offers no queue slots.

times.description: Posting times, `H:i` in the channel's time zone, at most 4 per day, no duplicates. Stored sorted.

timezone.description: IANA time zone of the channel. Posting times and queue slots are in this zone.

posting_goal.description: Posts per week the channel aims for.

posting_schedule.description: Seven days, Sunday first. `null` when the channel has no posting times (posts cannot use `queue`).

idea_stage_id.description: Stage (board column) of the idea. `null` is Unassigned.

position.description: Order within its stage, starting at 0.

ideas_count.description: Ideas in the stage. Only in `GET /idea-stages` and `PUT /idea-stages/order`.

MetricComparison.description: A metric for the range and for the previous range of the same length.

value.description: Value for the range. `null` when no channel in scope reports this metric.

change.description: Percent change from `previous` to `value`, rounded to 2 decimals. `null` when either is `null` or `previous` is 0.

AnalyticsDateRange.description: Calendar days in the API key user's time zone (both ends included).

AnalyticsAccountRef.description: Identity of a channel in an analytics row.

social_account_key.description: Stable analytics key of the channel. For a connected channel it is the social account id.

status.description: Current connection status. `null` when the channel is no longer in the workspace.

id.description: Analytics publication id. Read its detail with `GET /analytics/publications/{publication}`.

post_id.description: TryPost post, or `null` for a post made outside TryPost.

published_at.description: When the network published it, UTC, `Y-m-d H:i:s`.

media.description: The first image or video of the TryPost post, served by TryPost, or `null` for a post made outside TryPost or one without images or videos. Prefer it to `preview_metadata`: the networks' own thumbnail links expire.

AnalyticsSummary.description: Totals for the range compared with the previous range. `posts` counts posts published in the range (made in TryPost or not). `engagement_rate` is a percent. `watch_time_minutes` and `average_watch_time_seconds` cover videos.

followers.description: Followers at the end of the range. Unlike the other metrics, `change` is the difference in followers, not a percent. `value` is `null` when a connected channel in scope has no follower count for the range yet.

bounds.description: First and last day with analytics data in scope (`null` when there is none).

total.description: `null` when a connected channel in scope has no follower count for the range yet.

value.description: Followers at the end of the range.

growth.description: Followers gained between the first and last snapshot of the range.

net.description: Net followers gained in the range, when the network reports it.

series.description: One point per day: follower count of each channel, keyed by `social_account_key`.

resolution.description: Daily up to 14 days, weekly up to 90 days, monthly beyond. Weeks start on the API key user's start of week.

accounts.description: Channels with at least one post in the range.

top_posts.description: Up to 5 posts of the range with the most reactions, and up to 5 with the most comments.

performance.description: One row per channel with at least one post in the range, with each metric compared with the previous range.

coverage.description: How far back analytics have been collected for each connected channel. Each channel can have one row per collector.

ChannelInsightsFilters.description: The filters the server applied, after defaults.

sort.description: The sort used: the requested one when the channel reports that metric, else the first sortable metric it reports.

available_metrics.description: Metrics this channel reports, in display order (`followers`, `net_followers`, `posts`, `reactions`, `comments`, `engagement_rate`, `views`, `impressions`, `shares`, `reposts`, `quotes`, `saves`, `clicks`, `follows_gained`, `reach`, `watch_time_minutes`, `average_watch_time_seconds`).

summary.description: The workspace report shape, limited to this channel. Labels, untagged and types narrow the post metrics; followers stay account-wide.

metric_series.description: Per-bucket series for the range and the previous range. `posts`, `reach`, `views`, `impressions` and `profile_visits` are totals of the posts published in each bucket, not daily account totals. `followers` is the count at the end of each bucket; `net_followers` is cumulative from the start of the range.

resolution.description: Daily up to 92 days, weekly beyond (weeks start on the API key user's start of week).

values.description: Value of each metric in `metrics` for the bucket.
Value of each metric in `metrics` for the bucket.

growth.description: Monthly follower growth rate for the last 12 months. Ignores the range and the post filters. `null` until TryPost has at least two daily follower counts for the channel.

latest.description: Latest non-null monthly growth rate, in percent.

previous.description: Previous non-null monthly growth rate, in percent.

rank.description: Position by the `sort` metric, starting at 1.

post_id.description: TryPost post, or `null` for a post made outside TryPost.

media.description: The first image or video of the TryPost post, served by TryPost, or `null` for a post made outside TryPost or one without images or videos. `thumbnail_url` already prefers its image.

metrics.description: `null` for a metric the network does not report. `engagement_rate` is a percent.

content.description: Text inserted in the composer when the signature is picked.

me.description: What the API key's user may do in this workspace.

id.description: Key id (80 characters). Use it to delete the key.

WebhookEventType.description:
- `post.created`: a post was created. Its `data.status` is the status it was created with (`draft`, `scheduled`, `publishing` or `pending_approval`).
- `post.scheduled`: an existing post was scheduled (for example a draft scheduled, or a request approved). A post created already scheduled sends only `post.created`.
- `post.unscheduled`: a scheduled post went back to draft or to pending approval.
- `post.published`: the post was published.
- `post.failed`: publishing failed.
- `post.deleted`: a post was deleted. Not sent for posts imported from the network or removed by disconnecting their channel. Its `data` is only `{id, workspace_id}`.

status.description: `paused` is set by TryPost after 5 failed deliveries in a row (the account owner is emailed). Set `status: enabled` to resume.

signing_secret.description: Secret used to sign deliveries (`whsec_` and 32 characters). Only returned when you create, get or rotate the webhook.

id.description: Delivery id. It is also the `id` of the delivered body.

payload.description: The body that was sent: `{id, type, data, created_at}`. `data` is the post (`id, workspace_id, user_id, status, created_via, content, scheduled_at, published_at, created_at, updated_at, author, workspace, labels, media, platforms`), or `{id, workspace_id}` for `post.deleted`.

response_body.description: First 2000 bytes of the endpoint's answer, or the connection error.

attempts.description: Attempts made for this delivery (up to 3).

social_account_id.description: Social account of the workspace. Google Business is refused (its posts do not take video), and so is the source account.

content_type.description: Format to publish as. It must belong to the account's network and take video (for example `instagram_reel`, `tiktok_video`, `youtube_short`, `x_post`).

meta.description: Per-network settings, with the same rules as a post's `meta` (thread reply media by `url` is refused). On an active repurpose, the settings a network needs to publish are required, as on a scheduled post (for example TikTok `privacy_level`, Pinterest `board_id`, Discord `channel_id`, and a valid YouTube `description`).

source_social_account_id.description: Instagram or Facebook account watched for new videos. `null` when that account was removed.

source_account.description: The source account, `null` when it was removed. Returned by `GET /repurposes` (and by `PUT` on an active repurpose).

publish_mode.description: `publish` publishes each new video to the destinations; `draft` saves it as drafts.

paused_reason.description: Why TryPost paused it. `null` when it is not paused or you paused it.

activated_at.description: ISO 8601, UTC. Only videos posted after this instant are repurposed.

published_items_count.description: Items with status `published`. Items saved as drafts (`drafted`) are not counted. Only in `GET /repurposes`.

source_media_id.description: Id of the video on the source network.

reason.description: Why it was skipped or failed. `published_via_trypost`: the video was posted by TryPost, so it is not repurposed again.

posts.description: Posts created for this video, one per destination, with the network and its publishing state.

ContentTypeListing.description: Media and publishing rules of one content type.

forbids_mixed_media.description: Images and videos cannot be mixed in one post.

auto_fits_image.description: Images outside the aspect ratio are fitted instead of refused.

captionless.description: No text is sent (Instagram and Facebook stories), so the text is not measured for length or hashtags.

document_must_be_alone.description: A document (PDF) must be the only media of the post.

max_content_length.description: Text limit of the network in characters (code points). An X account with long posts gets 25000: read `max_content_length` on the social account.

max_hashtags.description: Most hashtags a post may carry (5 on Instagram), checked when the post is saved. `null` is no limit.

required_meta.description: `meta` keys needed to schedule or publish (TikTok `privacy_level`, Pinterest `board_id`, Discord `channel_id`). Settings that depend on others (a Google Business event) or that the text can stand in for (a YouTube title) are not listed.

recommended_content_length.description: Suggested text length for the network.

InstagramAudio.description: One Instagram audio asset: licensed music or an original sound. Send its `id` as `meta.audio.id` on an `instagram_reel`.

id.description: Instagram audio asset id. Send it as `meta.audio.id`.

artist.description: The artist, or for an original sound the creator's Instagram username.

cover_url.description: Cover art, or for an original sound the creator's profile picture. Instagram expires these links; read the track again with [Get Instagram audio](/api-reference/social-accounts/get-instagram-audio) for a fresh one.

duration_ms.description: Length of the track in milliseconds.

XPoll.description: An X poll: the post `content` (or the reply `text`) is the question, at most 280 characters even on an account with long posts. A poll carries no media, drafts included. A draft may lack the choices or the length; scheduling or publishing needs at least 2 choices, `duration_minutes` and a question. On update the poll is merged key by key with the stored one; `options` replaces the whole list.

options.description: 2 to 4 choices to schedule or publish, each 1 to 25 characters as X counts them (an emoji outside the basic plane, such as 🐧, counts two). No two the same, compared without case. Blank choices are dropped. More than 4, a repeated choice or one over 25 characters is refused on every save, drafts included.

duration_minutes.description: How long voting stays open, from 5 minutes to 7 days. Required to schedule or publish; there is no default.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Bodies: `Unauthenticated.` (no key, or a key that is invalid or revoked), `Token expired.` (past its `expires_at`), `Token not found.` and `No workspace selected.` (the key is no longer bound to a workspace).

Forbidden.description: The request is not allowed. API keys work only for workspace admins (the account owner or a member marked as admin): otherwise every request returns `Insufficient workspace permissions.`. Other bodies: `Workspace access denied.` (the key's user left the workspace) and `Personal access token required.` (an MCP OAuth token was sent) and `This action is unauthorized.` (the note belongs to another member).

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist in this workspace.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded. Limits: 60 requests per minute per workspace.

Conflict.description: Another change to this post or its channel's queue is in progress. Retry.

PaymentRequired.description: TryPost Cloud only: the workspace's account has no active subscription or trial. Body: `{"message": "Active subscription required."}`.
